The Research on Health Services and the International Health Institute for Maternal and Child Health at the Scientific Institute for Research, Hospitalization, and Healthcare (Burlo Garofolo) in Trieste, Italy, focuses on pediatrics, malnutrition, and infectious diseases. 2. Professor Malcolm E. Molyneux, affiliated with the College of Medicine at the University of Malawi in Blantyre, Malawi, specializes in malaria and research and practice in international tropical diseases. 3. Engineer Wisam Qarqash, from the Jordan Health Communication Partnership at Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health in Amman, Jordan, is an expert in the design, implementation, and evaluation of health communication programs. 4. Dr. Mahdi Ramsan Mohamed, from the Research Triangle Institute International in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, focuses on malaria control and prevention as well as neglected tropical diseases. 5. Dr. Rebecca Joyce Stoltzfus, from the Division of Nutritional Sciences at Cornell University in Ithaca, United States, specializes in international nutrition, public health, iron and vitamin A nutrition, and program research. 6. Ms. Carol Tom East, from the Central and Southern African Health Community in Arusha, Tanzania, is an expert in food fortification technical regulations, standards, and policy harmonization. 7. Dr. David Tovey, from The Cochrane Library and Cochrane Editorial Unit in London, United Kingdom, focuses on systematic reviews, health communications, and evidence for primary healthcare. 8. Ms. Vilma Qahoush Tyler, from the United Nations Children’s Fund Regional Office for Central and Eastern Europe and the Commonwealth of Independent States in Geneva, Switzerland, specializes in food fortification and public health programs. 9. Dr. Gunn Elisabeth Vist, from the Department of Preventive and International Health at the Norwegian Knowledge Centre for the Health Services in Oslo, Norway, is a methodologist specializing in systematic reviews and evidence assessment using GRADE. 10. Dr. Emorn Wasantwisut, from Mahidol University in Nakhon Pathom, Thailand, focuses on international nutrition, micronutrient biochemistry, and metabolism. 11. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, United States, contribute expertise in behavioral science and program evaluation. 12. Dr. Lynnette Neufeld, from the Monitoring, Learning, and Research division of the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition in Geneva, Switzerland, specializes in micronutrient programs and epidemiology. 13. Dr. Orishi Ebere Orisakwe, from the Toxicology Unit at the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Port Harcourt in Rivers State, Nigeria, focuses on pharmacology, food safety, and toxicology. 14. Professor Dalip Ragoobirsingh, from the University of the West Indies in Kingston, Jamaica, specializes in medical biochemistry, diabetology, diabetes education, and noncommunicable diseases. 15. Ms. Rusidah Selamat, from the Nutrition Division of the Department of Public Health at the Ministry of Health in Putrajaya, Malaysia, focuses on public health nutrition. 16. Dr. Maged Younes, from the Committee on World Food Security at the Food and Agriculture Organization in Rome, Italy, specializes in food safety, public health, and program management. 17. Dr. Robert J. Berry, from the Prevention Research Branch at the National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, United States, focuses on epidemiology, folate, and fortification. 18. Dr. Andreas Bluethner, from BASF SE in Limburgerhof, Germany, is an expert in fortificants and food fortification. 19. Dr. Julia Finkelstein, from the Division of Nutritional Sciences at Cornell University in Ithaca, United States, specializes in epidemiology and systematic reviews. 20. Dr. Elvira González de Mejía, from the Department of Food Science and Human Nutrition at the University of Illinois in Urbana, United States, focuses on fortification procedures and fortificants. 21. Dr. Jeff Gwirtz, from the Food Fortification Initiative in Manhattan, United States, specializes in milling and grain fortification. 22. Professor Richard Hurrell, from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) Institute of Food Science and Nutrition in Zurich, Switzerland, focuses on iron metabolism, bioavailability, and fortification. 23. Dr. Chowdhury Jalal, from Operations and Evaluation Research at Nutrition International in Ottawa, Canada, specializes in systematic reviews, micronutrient stability, and monitoring and evaluation. 24. Mr. Phillip J. Makhumula-Nkhoma, an independent consultant in Lilongwe, Malawi, focuses on legislation and regulatory affairs. 25. Dr. Luis A. Mejía, from the Department of Food Science and Human Nutrition at the University of Illinois in Urbana, United States, specializes in regulatory affairs. 26. Dr. Regina Moench-Pfanner, from the Nutrition Programmes division of the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN) in Geneva, Switzerland, focuses on food fortification and nutrition programs. 27. Dr. Helena Pachón, from the Food Fortification Initiative at Emory University in Atlanta, United States, is a nutrition scientist. 28. Mr. Peter Ranum, an independent consultant in Tucson, United States, specializes in industrial milling and fortification. 29. Mr. Georg Steiger, from DSM Nutritional Products in Kaiseraugst, Switzerland, focuses on fortificants, micronutrients, and biochemistry. 30. Dr. Parmi S. Suchdev, from the Department of Pediatrics and Global Health at Emory University in Atlanta, United States, specializes in pediatrics and global health. 31. Dr. Nancy Aburto Jennings, from the United Nations World Food Programme in Rome, Italy, and Dr. Arnaud Laillou, from the United Nations Children’s Fund in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, contributed as peer reviewers. 32. Dr. Diego Moretti, from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) Institute of Food Science and Nutrition in Zurich, Switzerland, and Ms. Becky Tsang, from the Food Fortification Initiative in Asia, based in Atlanta, United States, also served as peer reviewers. 33. External resource experts participated in technical presentations and discussions, providing factual information, feedback, and clarification when required. However, they did not participate in or influence the recommendations. 34. The acknowledgment of peer reviewers does not imply their endorsement of the recommendations in the guideline, nor does it necessarily represent the views, decisions, or policies of their affiliated institutions.
